Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators found.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta backend and defines only a normal console_scripts entry point.
  • entry_points.txt defines mysetuptool = mysetuptool.cli:main, which requires the user to run the command.
  • No setup.py, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, custom install/build hook, or malicious import-time execution evidence was found.
  • __init__.py only imports main from .cli and does not call main().

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential harvesting: no broad collection of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI/CD tokens, wallets, or similar secrets was identified.
  • Archive staging / exfiltration: no evidence of file harvesting, archive staging, external upload, webhook use, raw IP/C2 endpoint, or drop service usage was identified.
  • Persistence: no cron, systemd, launch agent, shell profile modification, startup registration, or background persistence loop was identified.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence of Kubernetes token use, Docker socket abuse, cloud metadata access, GitHub Actions token theft, or package publishing token reuse was identified.
  • Obfuscation/loader: no base64/zlib/marshal/eval/exec loader, obfuscation, dropper, or self-deleting payload was identified.
  • The GitHub-based “script update” features in mac_tool.py / ubuntu_tool.py and the Homebrew curl | bash installer appear to be user-selected menu actions. They are not tied to automatic execution, stealth, credential theft, or exfiltration in the provided evidence.
